title: Preparing a stay in the Gulf of Saint-Tropez with official brochures
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Brochures are most useful before arrival. They help spread the towns, balance travel time and avoid a series of days that all look alike.
content:
A brochure becomes truly useful before the stay, when you are still trying to balance harbours, villages, beaches, short walks and driving time. It does not need to be exhaustive to play that role well. It only needs to help distribute the territory more fairly.

Spread the towns instead of stacking them

Brochures help show that Saint-Tropez, Ramatuelle, Grimaud, Cogolin and La Garde-Freinet do not belong to the same register. Some days call for a harbour and animated streets, others for a hill village, a beach or a discreet valley. General documents prevent a stay made of places that feel too similar.

Choose one document for the day you want

A beach day or a cape walk does not require the same landmarks as a visit through an old village or a family outing. Official brochures help make that distinction before leaving, then point to the right PDF when needed, without getting lost in too many open files.

Keep the agenda separate

The brochure prepares the frame, but the agenda remains the last judge for events, markets, festivals and maritime appointments. The right method is to combine both: the brochure to build the day, the official agenda to confirm what is actually happening on the chosen date.
